sources.claim: Next recommends a restrictive image CSP and attachment disposition when serving SVG; enabling SVG alone does not establish missing protections.
The image response uses the configured CSP and disposition values. Empty CSP is not evidence of a restrictive policy; deployment may still add controls.

adversarial.rationale: Export-shaped comment text cannot configure the optimizer or clear its response policy.
Computed property identity stays unresolved rather than overriding known protective options.
Multiline literal configuration preserves all three explicitly unsafe header choices.

rules.false_positive_analysis: Advisory only. Trusted images or a reverse proxy can supply independent controls. SVG enablement alone, default/explicit protective CSP, attachment delivery, custom loaders, unoptimized images and output overrides stay silent.

sources.claim: Kestrel's nullable body-size property disables this limit when null; a finite default and independent per-request or proxy limits must be distinguished.
Resource-consumption limits are a CWE-400 control, but an absent local cap alone does not prove endpoint reachability or exploitable exhaustion.

adversarial.rationale: A comment cannot bind server options or disable a request-processing resource limit.
A comment inside the actual null assignment must not hide the explicit local limit opt-out.
An options parameter from another method does not establish the type of a similarly named field.

rules.false_positive_analysis: Advisory only. An independent cap or intentional streaming may justify this option. Require a locally bound standard options type and a flat literal configuration block; defaults, finite limits, reconfiguration, custom types and branching stay unresolved.

sources.claim: The package:http convenience API accepts a URI and header map; no TLS is inferred from a plain HTTP URI.
Bearer credentials require transport protection. A header declaration supports a local concern, not proof of the value or the deployed transport.

negative.source: const documentation = 'http://api.example.org/help';

adversarial.rationale: Dart block comments nest, so a source-like request after an inner closing marker is still comment data.
A multiline raw string is a single data literal; its embedded imports and calls are not executed.
Whitespace must not remove the direct binding between package:http, the URI and its Authorization header.
A spread may replace the header, so this bounded rule cannot establish the effective authentication map.

rules.false_positive_analysis: Local mock transports need review. Dart HTTP requires an imported package:http call, literal external HTTP URI and Authorization header; that variant is advisory. Loopback/private IPs, bare HTTP URL text, custom bindings and visible runWithClient overrides stay silent. Header values and cross-file overrides remain unverified; legacy FTP/Telnet signatures are unchanged.

sources.claim: Next requires a client entry boundary, not a directive in every transitive client component.
The directive belongs to React Server Components and follows the module import graph; ordinary client-rendered React does not need it.

adversarial.rationale: A comment mentioning a directive is not a module boundary and must not hide a genuine server-entry hook call.
An import and hook-shaped example inside a comment do not establish executable React usage.

adversarial.rationale: Source-shaped quoted text is documentation data, not an exported Next entry component or imported React hook.

rules.false_positive_analysis: Only a declared Next.js app page/layout entry with an imported React hook call is checked. Ordinary React apps, shared components inheriting a client import boundary, type-only imports, shadows, unknown frameworks and actual client directives stay silent. This is not a complete RSC module-graph analysis.

sources.claim: Authentication cookies expose an actual CookieBuilder policy; defaults differ from explicit insecure overrides.
None, not Never, disables Secure. SameAsRequest and Always are distinct policies and must not be conflated.

adversarial.rationale: A custom type alias cannot establish ASP.NET's authentication-cookie policy semantics.
An inline comment inside the actual configuration assignment does not change its unsafe literal value.

rules.false_positive_analysis: Names alone do not establish a credential. C# requires typed ASP.NET parameters and inline CookieOptions or a flat CookieAuthenticationOptions policy block with explicit HttpOnly=false. These variants are advisory because middleware can override flags; verify final headers.

rules.false_positive_analysis: Local development and upstream policy require review. C# requires typed ASP.NET parameters with inline Secure=false or a flat authentication-cookie SecurePolicy=None assignment. SameAsRequest, branches and unresolved changes stay silent; local policy is advisory, not final-header evidence.
